se.title: Pediatric Convulsive Status Epilepticus
se.subtitle: AES 2016 · Glauser et al · Epilepsy Currents 16(1):48-61

actions: ABCD: airway / breathing / circulation / disability (including neurologic exam)
Time seizure onset + monitor vital signs
Oxygen via NC / mask; consider intubation if respiratory status unstable
Fingerstick glucose; if < 60 mg/dL → age ≥2 yr: 2 mL/kg D25W IV | age <2 yr: 4 mL/kg D12.5W IV
IV access + electrolytes / CBC / tox screen / ASM levels

time_stages.subtitle: Choose one (IM midazolam / IV lorazepam / IV diazepam)
actions: IM Midazolam (preferred when no IV access): 13–40 kg → 5 mg; >40 kg → 10 mg (single dose)
IV Lorazepam: 0.1 mg/kg/dose (max 4 mg/dose; may repeat x1)
IV Diazepam: 0.15–0.2 mg/kg/dose (max 10 mg/dose; may repeat x1)
If none of the above are available: IV Phenobarbital 15 mg/kg (Level A, in-house code 2PHENO) / Rectal Diazepam 0.2–0.5 mg/kg, max 20 mg (Level B) / IN or buccal Midazolam (Level B)

time_stages.subtitle: Choose one, single dose
actions: IV Fosphenytoin 20 mg PE/kg (max 1500 mg PE) — not stocked in-house; substitute IV Phenytoin 20 mg/kg (Aleviatin, code 2DPH; rate ≤ 1 mg/kg/min)
If none of the above are available and not yet given: IV Phenobarbital 15 mg/kg (Level B)
All require continuous EEG monitoring + intubation + ICU

se.decision_label: Does Seizure Continue? — If yes → proceed to next stage; if stopped → symptomatic care
se.citation: Glauser T, Shinnar S, Gloss D, et al. Evidence-Based Guideline: Treatment of Convulsive Status Epilepticus in Children and Adults. Epilepsy Currents 2016;16(1):48-61.
